hints.content:
- A *translation* moves a figure up, down, left, or right, or any combination of those.
- A *rotation* turns a figure around a single point, either on or off of the figure.
- A *reflection* makes a mirror image of a figure across an imaginary line.
- A *dilation* enlarges or shrinks a figure.

For this figure, we can imagine holding a pencil on the paper near quadrilateral $A$ and turning the paper until quadrilateral $A$ overlaps quadrilateral $B$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: An image labeled B and pre-image labeled A of the same quadrilateral. A vertex of the pre-image is at 12 o clock and moves to 2 o clock on the image with an arrow curving from the pre-image's vertex to its corresponding vertex in the image. Another vertex is at 7 o clock and moves to 9 o clock with an arrow curving from that pre-image vertex to the image vertex. A point, where the pencil tip can be placed is to the bottom left of the pre-image.

hints.content: We apply a *rotation* to quadrilateral $A$ to get quadrilateral $B$.
